The patient's rapidly progressive gait disturbance and decreased sensation from the T3 dermatome downward, along with the presence of a diffusely enhancing lesion on MRI and an expansile bony lesion on CT, are highly suggestive of a metastatic spinal tumor. The absence of primary malignancy on CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis does not rule out this diagnosis, as some primary tumors may not be detectable at this stage.
